EmailTemplate.subject: MMC Program Info, ASU Cronkite School
EmailTemplate.textOnly:
{!Contact.Name},
Thank you for your interest in the Master of Mass Communication program at the Walter Cronkite School of Journalism and Mass Communication at Arizona State University! I look forward to helping you learn more about our graduate program. Is there a type or area of journalism/media you are most interested in?
About the Cronkite School Master's Programs The Cronkite School offers a Professional Master's Program centered around rel-world experiences that prepare students for careers in a rapidly evolving media industry. Degree options include a Master of Mass Communication (journalism) and an MA in Sports Journalism. Both degree programs are full-time, on-campus, and can be completed in as little as 12 months. Previous journalism experience is not necessary.
One of the highlights of our degree plan is the Cronkite Professional Experience in the last semester of the program. This experience immerses our students in their chosen area full-time, where they operate as a reporter, broadcaster, sports journalist, media professional or other role in their chosen field. By the end of the program, all students will have created a portfolio of professional-level journalistic work.
Read and experience more about the Cronkite School below: Master's Program Brochure Master's Program Website The Cronkite Journal
Media Partnerships and Career Services The Cronkite School partners with media corporations, foundations and other entities to publish and broadcast students' classwork at professional outlets, giving students a jumpstart on building professional portfolios for media careers. In addition to the university's career services, Cronkite School students have access to our very own career services director who specializes in the media and journalism fields.
Admission Students are admitted to start the program in the fall semester only. Applications should be submitted between September 1 and February 1 before the fall semester in which an applicant hopes to be admitted.
Our admission application requires submission of an online application, resume, personal statement, GRE scores, official undergraduate transcripts, three letters of recommendation, and a minimum score of 100 on the TOEFL exam (if an international student). A 3.0 undergraduate GPA is highly recommended, but not required. Prior journalism experience is not necessary.
The Campus Located in downtown Phoenix, The ASU Cronkite School is near major news organizations, sports venues, government agencies and cultural venues which enable our students to gain professional experience. Our building includes TV studios and control rooms, digital editing bays, computer labs and classrooms for students to learn in. Please contact me if you're interested in visiting the school and I will help coordinate your day.
I hope this information is helpful and please feel free to contact me if you have any additional questions.
Kindest regards,
Andrea Tang Academic Specialist | Arizona State University Walter Cronkite School of Journalism and Mass Communication 555 N. Central Ave. | Phoenix, AZ 85004 602.496.5056 | Andrea.Tang@asu.edu
